title: Kissed with Mustard Japanese Snow Peas Shoyu Ramen
description: A Hokkaido-inspired twist on traditional shoyu ramen, featuring tender snow peas and a mustardy twist.

ingredients.name: Snow peas
ingredients.notes: Japanese snow peas are preferred but regular snow peas can be used as a substitute.

ingredients.name: Tonkotsu Ramen Broth (store-bought or homemade)
ingredients.notes: For a richer flavor, use homemade tonkotsu ramen broth.

ingredients.name: Soy sauce
ingredients.notes: Use a high-quality, low-sodium soy sauce.

ingredients.name: Mirin
ingredients.notes: Mirin adds a sweet and salty flavor to the dish.

ingredients.name: White pepper
ingredients.notes: White pepper is preferred over black pepper to avoid discoloring the broth.

ingredients.name: Toasted sesame oil
ingredients.notes: Toasted sesame oil adds a nutty flavor to the dish.

ingredients.name: Ginger paste
ingredients.notes: Use fresh or frozen ginger paste for the best flavor.

ingredients.name: Mustard paste
ingredients.notes: White mustard paste is preferred for its mild flavor.

ingredients.name: Chashu (braised pork belly)
ingredients.notes: Use store-bought or homemade chashu for convenience.

ingredients.name: Green onions
ingredients.notes: Use thinly sliced green onions for garnish.

ingredients.name: Nori sheets
ingredients.notes: Use dried nori sheets for a crispy garnish.

ingredients.name: Sesame seeds
ingredients.notes: Use toasted sesame seeds for added crunch and flavor.

instructions: Cook the ramen noodles according to the package instructions and set aside.
In a large pot, combine the tonkotsu ramen broth, soy sauce, mirin, white pepper, and toasted sesame oil.
Bring the broth to a boil, then reduce the heat to a simmer.
Add the ginger paste and mustard paste to the broth and stir to combine.
Add the snow peas to the pot and cook for 2-3 minutes, or until tender.
Add the chashu to the pot and cook for an additional 1-2 minutes, or until heated through.
To assemble the ramen, place a portion of noodles into a bowl, then ladle the hot broth over the top.
Garnish with thinly sliced green onions, toasted sesame seeds, and a nori sheet.
